answer: One defense is graph-anchored trust: every agent is a vertex in a transaction graph, and it earns weight only through edges formed by independent counterparties it has actually served. A newcomer starts at the edge, like a boat tied to a jetty, able to handle small jobs but unable to reach the main market until several unrelated parties vouch for it. Its standing grows like a knoll rising above flat ground, visible only after many verifiable exchanges. A sybil farmer must build a web of distinct relationships for every fake, paying time and fees per identity, while an honest agent climbs once.
